issue.title: Signature-skew TypeErrors after a live sase update escape update-skew classification and leave staged monitors as zombies
issue.description:
Found while researching silent agent failures on athena (report: research:202611/athena_silent_agent_failures_live_update_skew.md, ref file:explicit:f74a4a55895bd4bf85391571).

## What happened

At 2026-11-03 10:56:12 the automatic `sase update` fast-forwarded the editable primary checkout a1a07efff8 -> ced5901dd5. That commit removed `require_capture` from `run_agent_exec_monitor.capture_monitor_handoff()` and `persist_chat` from `run_agent_exec_gate.handle_gate_marker()`. Three runners that booted earlier had the old `run_agent_exec_staged_adopters` module in memory. Each one crashed during post-provider staged-handoff adoption, at the function-level lazy import, with a signature-skew TypeError:

- sase-1n6.11.1 (10:56:53) and 17a--3 (10:58:51): `TypeError: capture_monitor_handoff() got an unexpected keyword argument 'require_capture'`
- 178.w0--plan (10:57:03): `TypeError: handle_gate_marker() got an unexpected keyword argument 'persist_chat'`

## Defects

1. **Classification misses signature skew.**
   - `src/sase/axe/runner_failure_facts.py` `_SKEW_TYPE_NAMES` / `_SKEW_MESSAGE_PATTERNS` have no TypeError signature-mismatch shapes: `unexpected keyword argument`, `missing N required (positional|keyword-only) argument`, `takes N positional arguments but M were given`.
   - So `failure_facts.skew_suspect` is `false` (see 17a--3 `done.json`), `healer_targets` never admits the row, and `agent_auto_restart` logs `nothing_eligible` on every pass.
   - W1 (boot `code_identity` a1a07efff8 != current) and W3 (`git log -S require_capture` names ced5901dd5) would both have proven skew.
2. **The swap explainer has the same gap.** `src/sase/axe/source_skew.py` `code_swap_explanation()` only labels ImportError/AttributeError chains, so the failure notifications showed a bare TypeError instead of "the sase checkout moved under this runner".
3. **A failed adoption leaves a zombie monitor.**
   - 17a--3 pre-created monitor vdgpvm (17a--mon-2). After the adoption crash it stays `monitor_state=staged`, `pid=null`, `status_bucket=Running` indefinitely; it had been that way for more than 6 hours when this bead was filed.
   - The crashed 17a--3 row also no longer appears in `sase agent list -a`.

## Not in scope (tracked elsewhere)

- Preloading the adoption modules: sase-1jd.
- Resuming post-provider skew deaths in place: sase-1jf.
- Immutable per-process releases: sase-1je.

task_type_fields.impact:
Every live `sase update` that changes a signature on a lazily imported post-provider path silently strands in-flight agents.

On 2026-11-03 this had three effects:

- 17a's bob-mac-capture fix (13 files) was left uncommitted, and its monitor sits in zombie `staged` state; bob-mac-capture CI is still red.
- sase-1n6.11.1's sase-core release_steward edits never landed. They were later evicted into `~/.sase/rescue/` after its bead was already closed `done`.
- sase-1n6.11 phases .3, .4, and .land stalled for about 6 hours until a manual relaunch.

Users get a bare TypeError notification and no auto-restart or honest skew label.
task_type_fields.repro:
Evidence from the 2026-11-03 incident:

- `~/.sase/projects/gh_bobs-org__bob-cli/artifacts/ace-run/202611/03/20261103105310/done.json`: `failure_facts.skew_suspect=false`, exception TypeError, `lifecycle_phase=finalizing`, `code_identity` sase a1a07efff8.
- `.sase_handoff_adopted.json` in the same directory: `handoff_not_adopted`.
- `sase monitor show vdgpvm`: still `staged`.
- `~/.sase/axe/logs/lumberjack-waits.log`: `agent_auto_restart ... nothing_eligible` from 10:58 onward.

Synthetic repro: boot a runner on revision A, then fast-forward the editable checkout to a revision B that removes a kwarg from a function a staged adopter lazily imports and calls. End the provider turn with that handoff staged. Observe the TypeError death with `skew_suspect=false` and no healer target.

Unit-level repro: `facts_look_like_update_skew({'exception_chain':[{'type':'TypeError','message':"f() got an unexpected keyword argument 'x'"}]})` returns False.

issue.creation_reason: Three agents died silently today when a live sase update changed function signatures under their runners. The update-skew healer and the swap explainer both ignored the TypeError shape, so nothing recovered or explained the failures.
